bounds: One runtime with five effective availability states and separate load, outcome and finally phases. The failure count saturates at the first 30-second delay, so repeated capped failures can continue without a bound on attempt count. Logical ticks count whole elapsed seconds. A wall-clock change is a stutter.
fairness: The host load and its finally callback must settle. The monotonic clock must advance to exhaust a pending cooldown.
limitations: Service replacement during recovery and concurrent runtimes require their separate lifecycle ownership models.

The model projects wall-clock changes away and uses elapsed seconds. The SQLite/runtime regression checks both wall-clock directions and the exact millisecond retry boundary, including repeated capped delays.
Exceptions from diagnostics and cross-process restart are outside this recovery projection.

assumptions: No scheduling fairness. External availability changes are restricted to idle states.
The host service load eventually resolves or rejects and its finally callback runs.
Weak fairness of monotonic elapsed-time ticks while a cooldown is active.
No scheduling fairness. A cooldown can persist while elapsed time does not advance.
